clue.text: Fatally well-directed

parts.note: a shot aimed so well that it kills: 'fatally' gives the lifeless part, 'well-directed' the accurate part, together an idiom for exactly right

explanation.surface: A description of a marksman's deadly accurate shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely accurate, and a fatal, well-aimed shot is literally that.

clue.text: An engagement in a Norfolk community leads to frustrations

indicators.note: the engagement is placed inside the Norfolk town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England
an appointment is an engagement or arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A date in a small Norfolk town ends in letdowns.
explanation.walkthrough: DISS is a small market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England; 'leads to' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointments are setbacks that frustrate one's hopes, so the plural synonym fits.

clue.text: Shopping centres, by Milton

definitions.meaning: covered walkways lined with shops
the title of a masque written by John Milton

explanation.definitionFit: Covered shopping passages are called this, and Milton wrote a pastoral entertainment of that title.

clue.text: A boy in livery is a formidable opponent

definitions.meaning: an old term for a smartly uniformed young groom or servant
a fierce, aggressive competitor

explanation.definitionFit: Historically a liveried boy servant had this name; a ferocious rival is likened to the big cat.

clue.text: The notoriety of calenders

indicators.note: read as 'made out of', the definition is formed from the letters of the next word rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on the bad reputation of cloth-pressing machines.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue with a very light anagram signal: 'of' says the answer is built out of the letters of 'calenders' (machines for pressing cloth).
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for a scandal or public scene, hence notoriety.

clue.text: A song from Lehar I admire

indicators.note: the song is taken from within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A fan praises a number by the operetta composer Lehar.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song in an opera, a natural item from an operetta composer.

clue.text: A hard worker, one not above suspicion

definitions.meaning: British slang for someone who toils diligently
slang for a person who takes bribes or profits corruptly

explanation.walkthrough: In British English the word praises a diligent toiler; in American usage it names a corrupt official, hence suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the word means both a diligent toiler and a corrupt profiteer.

clue.text: Annoy somebody-as a ballet dancer one must!

definitions.meaning: to offend or upset another person

definitions.text: as a ballet dancer one must
definitions.meaning: literally, a dancer en pointe walks on the tips of the feet

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to offend someone, and literally describes a dancer on point.

clue.text: Fabric for dismissal

definitions.meaning: coarse cloth used for sacks
being fired from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sack cloth and being fired from a job share this name.

clue.text: Raised to great heights, having taken the air

definitions.meaning: exalted, stirred to brilliance
breathed in

explanation.definitionFit: Means both creatively exalted and, literally, having breathed in.

clue.text: Trick obtained by a hand without trumps

definitions.meaning: a deception or subterfuge
a bridge term for a hand holding no trump cards

explanation.definitionFit: Means trickery or chicanery, and in bridge a hand void of trumps.

clue.text: Dull traveller on foot

definitions.meaning: uninspired, prosaic
someone walking

explanation.definitionFit: As adjective it means prosaic and plodding; as noun it names a walker.

clue.text: A collection of animals, set at intervals

definitions.meaning: a group of horses kept for breeding
to dot or ... a surface with items

explanation.definitionFit: A breeding establishment for horses, and the verb meaning to dot or scatter across a surface.

clue.text: Left helpless so wired?

definitions.meaning: marooned with no means of getting away
a wire made of twisted strands

explanation.definitionFit: Means marooned and helpless, and describes cable twisted from several strands.

clue.text: Income needing shillings before both ends meet

indicators.note: the shillings letter goes in front of the rest

parts.note: s. is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money
one end of something is its tip
the other is its end; the two words placed together meet

explanation.surface: Someone on a salary struggles to make ends meet and needs a few more shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the idiom 'make both ends meet'; 'meet' just sets the two words for an end side by side, and s. is old pre-decimal British shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular payment such as a clergyman's salary is a form of income.

clue.text: Bear in mind to go into a Scottish town

parts.note: to enter is to go into
Tain is a town in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: Advice to remember to visit a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: TAIN is a small town on the Dornoch Firth in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an idea is to hold it in one's mind or consider it.

clue.text: A bit of ancient Ur installed in Italy

indicators.note: only a portion of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: A fragment of the old Mesopotamian city is put on display in an Italian museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ur installed in' looks like a container, but the city sits in the letters of 'ancient Ur installed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city in Piedmont, in the north-west of that country.

clue.text: Suitable condition of life in a wall

definitions.meaning: a position or role that suits a person
a recess in a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable fitting role in life, and a shallow recess in a wall for ornaments.

clue.text: Act at an organised musical work

indicators.note: the letters of the three short words are arranged into new order

explanation.surface: Performers stage a piece of music at an event.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition with solos and chorus, a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Laundry of E. England

definitions.meaning: a batch of clothes being washed
a large square bay on the east coast of England

explanation.walkthrough: The bay is the shallow inlet of the North Sea between Lincolnshire and Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: A load of washing, and the bay between Lincolnshire and Norfolk on England's east coast.

clue.text: Plot H.L.I. devised in eminence

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Highland Light Infantry, a former Scottish regiment

explanation.surface: Scottish soldiers hatch a scheme on a high point.
explanation.walkthrough: H.L.I. was the Highland Light Infantry, a British army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a piece of high ground, such as the summit of a hill.

clue.text: The rich source I have

definitions.meaning: a plentiful supply, as of ore or information
belonging to me

explanation.definitionFit: A rich source of minerals or facts, and the possessive pronoun for something I own.

clue.text: Pupils on the march identified fauna

definitions.meaning: British schoolchildren walking in a double file
large reptiles of rivers

explanation.walkthrough: A school crocodile is a British term for children walking in pairs in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a two-by-two file of schoolchildren has this name; the reptiles are animal life.

clue.text: Remedies for odd people, so to speak

definitions.meaning: treatments that heal
old slang for eccentric characters

explanation.definitionFit: Treatments that heal, and an old slang word for eccentric oddballs.

clue.text: Go by — or don't go at all

definitions.meaning: move past
decline one's turn, as in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: To move past something, or to decline a turn and make no bid in cards.

clue.text: Profit returns to an artist-and falls

indicators.note: the word for profit is read backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a common abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's money comes back, and then the market tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like a verb but names the waterfall; RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, known simply by this name plus falls.

clue.text: I trod badly-shaken to the dancing-party

indicators.note: a shaken jumble of letters, signalling they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous guest stumbles on the way to a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A ridotto was an 18th-century public assembly with music and dancing, often masked.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian-derived term for a public ball or masked dance, a dancing-party.

clue.text: Standard arrangements that could produce Spartan distress

indicators.note: rearranging the answer's letters would give the following words, so they are rearranged back

explanation.surface: Battle banners sorted so as to express Spartan distress.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs in reverse: the answer rearranged produces 'Spartan distress'.
explanation.definitionFit: The national flag of the United States, a standard being a flag or banner.
